title: The little girl who played for money and with a union band
summary: As a child she played for teas and neighbours, charging a dollar an hour. At 10 or 12 she played with a union band by ear without reading, and musicians took her out with her mother's trust.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Once you got to Pittsburgh do you remember early years of playing piano?
I never stopped playing piano. I had a cousin

that used to dance and we'd make a little money dancing. At one time when I was about 6 or 7 years old I made more money than my stepfather by this. The teachers used to take me home with them and give me a little handkerchief pocket full of money. I'd play for the (musician?), they'd give a little afternoon tea. I'd have to sit on someone's lap, I was so small. I'd play for the little teas and for the neighborhood. I'd charge a dollar an hour.

All requests. I couldn't read piano and - well, this is getting a little ahead of it, but I'll talk about it now while it's on my mind. When I was 10 or 12 I played with a union band there and tunes like "The Doll Dance" I couldn't read it but I had such a terrific ear that after they played the first chorus, I knew it. They'd have the music up in front of me and I never even told them I couldn't read it. But it must have been all right and no complaints because I was hired from year to year to play with them.
Were you a member of the union?

No. The strangest thing happened after the musicians found out that I was playing with them. They used to come by the house, when I was between the ages of 8 and 10 or 12, when I was in grade school, and take me out. and pick me up mother, a I had a family that didn't mind. In the beginning they had an older member to go with me and after a while some
musician would get her confid_ence, gain her confidence and then she'd allow me to go with them.
